A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same aLoRA work. Their text, equations, Figures 1–10, Tables 1–2, and Appendices A–H are available and support reliable comparison despite reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original inference-timing experiments, seven-task finetuning comparisons, and evaluations of uncertainty quantification, answerability, query rewriting, and jailbreak detection.

after.justification: v5 retains these original timing, finetuning, and intrinsics results, including the calibration result in Appendix G.1.

M1.justification: Selective activation in Equation 6, cache reuse, invocation handling, and SFT remain unchanged. The added QLoRA and DoRA discussion concerns compatibility and potential extensions, without revising the proposed aLoRA procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven SFT tasks and the same intrinsics training and evaluation coverage. Appendices F–H retain the dataset lists, task definitions, and test scenarios.

E2.justification: LoRA remains the comparator in the timing, SFT, and intrinsics experiments. QLoRA, DoRA, and additional prompt-tuning literature are discussed in v5 but are not added to the reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Splits, metrics, hyperparameter searches, training budgets, and timing procedures are retained. The LoRA rank-8 versus aLoRA rank-32 timing setting emphasized in v5 Section 3 was already documented in v3 Appendix E.

E4.justification: Section 4.1 adds a brief qualitative analysis of the existing hyperparameter search, reporting no systematic difference between methods in performance-maximizing rank. The timing rank-sensitivity discussion and out-of-distribution jailbreak evaluation were already present.

E5.justification: Both retain the same two-sided t-test with p = 0.8 and the three timing batches described in Appendix E. Seed information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Figures 3–8 and Appendix G.1 are unchanged, including all 56 accuracy entries in Figure 4. Section 4.1 newly reports the qualitative finding that neither method consistently required higher or lower rank.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the cache-equivalence and inference-cost propositions, and their Appendix C proofs are retained. The new verbal clarification of cache terminology adds explanation without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central claims of cache reuse, competitive accuracy, and lower inference costs remain. The abstract changes the software contribution from supplementary code to reported Hugging Face PEFT integration, and the conclusion explicitly qualifies higher-rank efficiency claims with increased training costs.

C2.justification: v5 adds quantization compatibility conditions, explains the incompatibility between selective activation and merging adapter weights into the base model, and acknowledges higher-rank training costs. The QLoRA and DoRA discussion also identifies extensions beyond the demonstrated experiments.

D1.justification: v5 reports PEFT integration, identifies TRL SFTTrainer, provides a location for the modified vLLM implementation, and states that quantized implementation support exists. The detailed settings in the appendices are retained.

R1.justification: v5 adds discussion and citations for QLoRA, DoRA, He et al.'s parameter-efficient transfer-learning comparison, PEFT, and TRL. These extend positioning relative to prompt tuning and adapter variants without substantially redefining the research contribution.

P1.justification: There are localized explanatory additions, copyedits, and changes to headings and citation style. The main section sequence and Appendix A–H organization remain, with most prose retained.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted into NeurIPS style, changing page geometry, title treatment, running headers, heading typography, spacing, and figure/table placement throughout. Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–2 retain their designs and content; the major change concerns the overall layout.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3, v5 provides clearer implementation access and training-library information, better positioning against related adapter approaches, and useful compatibility and training-cost qualifications. These improve usability and interpretation while retaining the original empirical and theoretical support. The added extensions remain untested, so the overall gain is limited.
